title: Reported counterexample: more stored ion energy can still fail the same withdrawal operation
statement: The supplied finite-model checks reportImax=150pA+NaV suppression200s returning to the model healthy basin after ordinary ATPase support, whileImax=100pA600s relapses despite storing more gradient energy. The ordinary restored-ATPase comparator succeeds without light. These are source-reported ODE outcomes and accounts, not whole-audited integrations or biological recovery.

requires: Actual declared finite-cell equations, same finite-stock injury, uncalibrated pure-Na law and stated imposed-control/ordinary-handoff histories; supplied saved cases are model data.
Current labels150/100/350pA are Imax parameters of the added law, not measured or constant actual photocurrents.

assumptions: Source-reported numerical checks only: no completed whole ODE audit or replay by intake, acquired sustained pump, tissue viability or clinical threshold. Native transient dose is not a converged physical prediction.
costs: Gross turnover and productive photons, repeated passive Na reentry, explicit later ATPase work and all actual expression/retinal/optical/blocker costs. No acquired incident-light dose or safety account.
contract.units: Currents pA, times s, energy nJ, ion/ATP counts fmol; reported model-basin classifier is Boolean and distinct from biological recovery.
contract.obstruction: End-of-light thresholds and total stored energy do not order post-withdrawal recoverability in the reported model.

body: Use the same closed-bath600s ATPase-off state and read the final1800s post-light/NaV-restored/ATPase-active classifier. Do not use first_sampled_ionic_return_after_handoff_s=0 as success. The supplied tighter BDF/Radau cases report controlledImax=150pA stored gain0.365377nJ versus failedImax=100pA0.417412nJ; gross productive-photon lower bounds are59.357152nJ versus116.528312nJ. The nativeImax=350pA replays agree on final basin but change precise photon dose from roughly80.8nJ to77.1nJ on refinement, so the precise native dose remains unconverged. No same-photon advantage over optical ATP or ordinary supported recovery is established.
